Walking Intervention — Pre/Post
⚠ DATA CORRECTION (2026-09-26, re-run complete)
Six sessions had duplicated / mixed-up BIDS data (sub-034/065/074/084/091 ses-02, sub-089 ses-01); two further subjects (sub-056, sub-057) are excluded pending archive re-acquisition. FastSurfer / fMRIPrep / XCP-D and all FC/EC features and statistics were re-run on the corrected data (an earlier re-extraction attempt had silently failed; it was re-run and verified before this report). Headline changes: the subcortical-volume finding is NULL (0 FDR-significant; the previously reported 7 were an artifact); the EC picture is now limbic → cerebellum (replicated across four cerebellum divisions and rDCM/VAR/Granger); FC Motor_L remains the top FC effect.

Walking Intervention vs Control — Multimodal Results

Preliminary · 53 structural subjects (105 sessions) / 44 FC-EC subjects (85 obs) / ~39 voxelwise · all group×time interactions · FDR or cluster-corrected · effective connectivity via rDCM/VAR/Granger/K-SG TE · cerebellum divided 4 ways (single node / Buckner-7 / King-10 / functional zones)

Headline (corrected 2026-09-26, re-run complete): after fixing 6 sessions with duplicated/mixed-up BIDS data, the subcortical-volume finding is null (0 FDR-significant structures). Cortical thickness is unchanged. The previously-reported "volume preservation" was driven by the duplicated subjects. The surviving signals are functional/effective-connectivity: reduced Motor_L whole-brain coupling in walkers (FC) and a limbic → cerebellum directed effect that replicates across all four cerebellum divisions and across rDCM/VAR/Granger (EC).

Interpretation

No structural effect survives correction. After excluding the duplicated/mixed-up sessions, none of the 10 subcortical structures, DKT regions, or cortical-thickness maps shows a group×time interaction (top trend Right-Thalamus q=0.15). Two readings: (i) a short walking intervention is unlikely to change gross subcortical volume — structural change on this timescale is biologically implausible — so the null is the expected result; (ii) the study is only powered for large effects (n=53, 105 sessions). The functional/effective-connectivity effects reported in the FC/EC tabs therefore carry the intervention signal, not macro-structure. The earlier "volume preservation" claim should not be cited.

Outlier screen

Two control subjects show large negative deltas: sub-063 (73F; L/R hippocampus −284/−257 mm³, z≈−3.6 both; its ICV also changed +7.2% between sessions, suggesting segmentation instability) and sub-077 (70F; left amygdala −232 mm³, z=−3.2). A third case, sub-067 (Walking), has mild bilateral MTL atrophy consistent with age. Refitting the LMM without sub-063+077 (n=51) or without all six flagged subjects (n=47) keeps 0 FDR-significant structures (top q=0.21 / 0.28), so the structural null does not depend on these subjects.

Functional connectivity

Atlas = Schaefer400 (400 cortical parcels, Yeo 7 networks) + Tian subcortex + 10 cerebellar = 442 parcels — not Glasser (Glasser only used in the subdivided-ROI robustness check).
Design: n=85 observations = 44 two-session subjects; LMM value ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject), BH-FDR. Fisher-z matrices from fc-variant XCP-D denoised BOLD (aCompCor, bandpass 0.01–0.08 Hz). Robustness: Motor_L whole-brain is unaffected by outliers (it strengthens when subject 088 is removed); DLPFC_R whole-brain weakens (p 0.035→0.060) and is reported as fragile.

20 significant (q<0.05) of 489 tests (fc variant; 8 in the GSR robustness variant). Outlier screen

3 flagged subject×metric deltas (|z|>3 within group) among the significant FC effects. 3 of 20 tested effects change materially when flagged subjects are removed: Motor_L strengthens (p 0.0004→0.0003), DLPFC_R whole-brain weakens past FDR (0.035→0.060). No FC effect is driven solely by a single outlying subject.

Interpretation

Walkers show reduced left-motor-cortex whole-brain coupling after training relative to controls. The partial correlation effect is small in absolute units but the most robust FC finding (survives GSR, both FD thresholds, and outlier exclusion). Two plausible readings: (i) reduced redundancy — motor regions become more selectively coupled after training; (ii) a shift from broad sensorimotor co-activation toward task-relevant subnetworks. The cerebellum–subcortical and cerebellum-internal effects (visible only with finer divisions) suggest the cerebellum participates in the reconfiguration — in the subdivided analysis, walkers specifically increased coupling of left cerebellar lobule VI superior and Crus I anterior (sensorimotor/learning cerebellum) with the rest of the brain. All FC effects are diffuse at the edge level (NBS null) and should be read as system-level tendencies, not focal network changes.

Effective connectivity

Directed connectivity on network nodes from the 442-parcel (Schaefer400+Tian+cerebellar) ec-variant denoised BOLD (0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing). The connectome always contains the 7 Yeo cortical networks (Vis, SomMot, DorsAttn, SalVentAttn, Limbic, Cont, Default) + Subcortical; only the cerebellum representation changes, so results can be compared across parcellation choices: cerebellum as 1 node (9 nodes total; 72 directed edges), Buckner-7 cerebellar networks (15 nodes; 210 edges), King-10 cerebellar parcels (18 nodes; 306 edges), functional zones (Motor/Cognitive/Vestibular; 11 nodes; 110 edges). n=44 subjects (85 obs); LMM per edge ~ group×time + Age + Gender + (1|subject), BH-FDR within division×method. TR=0.8 s → HRF-latency confounded; hypothesis-generating, non-causal.

What are Region1…10? (King-2019 annotation)

The 10 cerebellar parcels (labels 433–442, King et al. 2019 via PennLINC 4S456) have no per-region network names in the label file. We annotate each region by (i) majority overlap with the Buckner-7 cerebellar functional atlas (Yeo-aligned networks), (ii) DiFuMo functional zone, and (iii) its own dominant FC target (mean Fisher-z to the 7 Yeo cortical networks across all subjects). R5 is the cerebellar control-network region; R7–R10 are default-network regions; R1–R2 sensorimotor; R3–R4 salience/ventral-attention.

Network-to-network effect matrices (per method × map)

Directed group×time t for every method × cerebellum map; rows = target, columns = source (same A[target, source] convention as rDCM/VAR); blue = negative, red = positive; * = FDR q<0.05. Node order is identical in every panel: 7 Yeo networks + Subcortex + the cerebellum nodes of that map (King-10 regions annotated, e.g. R5 (Cont)). Full tables: ec/stats/matrices/ec_matrix_long.csv and ec_matrix_<method>_<map>.csv.

Reading the matrices: the negative (blue) block in the Limbic row / cerebellum columns in every map is the limbic→cerebellum effect; the red cells in the cerebellum rows / SomMot–DorsAttn–Cont columns are cerebellum→cortical effects; the King-10 panel shows they split across the annotated regions (R1–R3 limbic targets, R2/R5 cortical sources).

EC NBS (cluster-level)

No significant subnetworks (NBS, 5,000 permutations, |t|≥2.5 & 3.0) in any of the 8 division×method connectomes. Largest components (t=3.0 / t=2.5): 1-node rDCM 1 edge p=0.21 / 2 edges p=0.22; VAR 1/2 p=0.22; Buckner-7 rDCM 2 edges p=0.16, VAR 2/4 p=0.16/0.25; King-10 rDCM 0/4 p=0.38, VAR 3 edges p=0.11; zones 0–1 edges. Like the FC ROI-to-ROI NBS, EC changes are diffuse — individual edges survive FDR, coherent edge-clusters do not.

Outlier screen

6 flagged subject×edge deltas (|z|>3) among the significant EC effects (subjects 047, 076, 063, 079, 071; single edges each). Removing them leaves the headline limbic → cerebellum effects unchanged; two secondary MDTB edges weaken past FDR (Region9→SomMot 0.021→0.055; Region1→Region4 0.034→0.063) and are marked fragile.

Interpretation

Direction of effects (delta = post − pre): controls increased limbic→cerebellar influence (+0.037) while walkers decreased it (−0.020); conversely walkers increased cerebellar→sensorimotor (+0.039 vs −0.022) and cerebellar→dorsal-attention influence (+0.007 vs −0.038). Reading: the walking intervention is associated with a re-balancing of cerebellar communication — stronger cerebellar output to sensorimotor/attention networks, weaker limbic input to the cerebellum. This pattern is anatomically coherent with cerebellar engagement in gait and motor learning, and with the known limbic/cerebellar coupling in ageing. Because BOLD effective-connectivity at TR=0.8 s cannot separate neural lag from HRF latency, these are hypothesis-generating; spectral DCM or task-based paradigms would be needed for causal claims.

Whole-brain voxelwise

Signal-amplitude / entropy maps (not connectivity). Seed-to-voxel connectivity is in the FC tab (separate from the ROI-to-ROI matrices).

ALFF / ReHo

Convergent group×time cluster in left visual cortex (cluster-corrected p<0.05), old cohort — these maps still predate the BIDS correction and will be re-run with the corrected cohort.

Structural connectivity (dMRI)

Pending. QSIPrep preprocessing was ~98/108 complete at report time; QSIRecon (SS3T + ACT-hsvs) and the connectome matrices have not yet been generated. This tab will be populated when the dMRI pipeline completes.

Methods

Cohort & design

Longitudinal walking intervention, 2 groups (Walking vs Control) × 2 timepoints (pre = ses-01, post = ses-02). All models estimate the group×time interaction (differential change between groups). Mean-FD > 0.3 mm excluded.

Preprocessing

  • fMRIPrep 25.2.5 (MNI152NLin6Asym res-2; no recon-all)
  • XCP-D 26.0.2 — fc variant: aCompCor, FD scrubbing (>0.3mm), bandpass 0.01–0.08 Hz, 6 mm smoothing; ec variant: aCompCor, bandpass 0.01–0.1 Hz, 0 mm smoothing. Confounds regressed at this stage; no re-regression downstream.
  • FastSurfer 2.5.4 for subcortical volumes / cortical thickness

Functional connectivity

442-parcel atlas (Schaefer400 + Tian subcortex + 10 cerebellar). Three separate analysis families: (i) ROI-to-ROI — 442×442 Fisher-z matrices (97,461 edges, NBS), 489-test metric tournament, and block-level metrics across every cerebellum map × estimator (Pearson/Spearman/partial on the block-mean timeseries; LMM ~ group×time + Age + Gender + mean_fd + (1|subject)); (ii) seed-to-voxel — per-subject delta maps, FSL randomise TFCE (5,000 perms); (iii) whole-brain voxelwise (ALFF/ReHo, own tab). The block-level division comparison uses the ec-variant block timeseries (shared with EC) for comparability; the 442-parcel metric tournament uses the fc variant.

Effective connectivity

Block timeseries are built from the corrected 442-parcel ec timeseries by script/build_block_timeseries.py. Every connectome contains the 7 Yeo cortical networks + subcortex; only the cerebellum representation differs: cerebellum as 1 node (9 nodes; 72 directed edges), Buckner-7 (the cerebellum split into its 7 Yeo-like networks via the Buckner 2011 2 mm atlas; 15 nodes; 210 edges), King-10 (the 10 King et al. 2019 cerebellar regions, labels 433–442 of the 442 atlas; 18 nodes; 306 edges), functional zones (Motor/Cognitive/Vestibular via DiFuMo cerebellar component classes; 11 nodes; 110 edges). Cerebellar Yeo/zone blocks are voxel-level BOLD means over the respective mask; cortical/subcortical blocks are parcel means of the 442 timeseries. Every method is run on every representation (method × map matrix): VAR(1) A-matrix (multivariate linear, OLS), rDCM (regression dynamic causal modelling, TAPAS/Julia, Wiener stochastic input, 16 samples/TR, run on HPC), pairwise Granger (bivariate F-statistic; block-level across all maps plus a seed-based variant), KSG transfer entropy (kNN, k=4) plus a binned plug-in TE. King-10 regions are annotated with their dominant Yeo network by majority Buckner-7 overlap (script/annotate_king10.py). Edge-wise LMM + BH-FDR within map×method; NBS cluster correction applied to every representation (all null). All are HRF-latency confounded at TR=0.8 s → hypothesis-generating.

Outlier screen

For every FDR-significant feature in every family (FC metrics, EC edges), per-subject post−pre deltas were z-scored within group and |z|>3 flagged; the LMM was refit without flagged subjects (script/outlier_check.py; outputs shared/outlier_flags.csv, shared/outlier_robustness.csv). Structural outliers were screened separately (sub-063 hippocampal loss + ICV instability, sub-077 amygdala loss, sub-067 age-consistent MTL atrophy, sub-099 large ICV, sub-093 borderline putamen — all retained; see the Structural tab outlier screen for the robustness refits).

Voxelwise / seed-to-voxel

ALFF/ReHo (voxelwise), seed-to-voxel Pearson→Fisher-z. Per-subject delta (post−pre) maps; two-sample t-test via FSL randomise, TFCE, 5000 permutations. Cluster composition via FSL atlasq + AAL3v1 (covers cortex, subcortex and cerebellum).

Corrections & caveats

  • BIDS correction (2026-09-25): 6 sessions re-converted from DICOM (sub-034/065/074/084/091 ses-02, sub-089 ses-01); sub-056/057 excluded (ses-02 not their own scans). FastSurfer, fMRIPrep, XCP-D and all downstream FC/EC features were re-run on the corrected data. The first re-extraction attempt silently failed (process-pool OOM); it was re-run serially and verified before the analyses in this report.
  • BH-FDR within families; NBS cluster-level FWER (5,000 perms) for full ROI-to-ROI (FC) and all EC divisions; TFCE for voxelwise.
  • LMM fitted with BFGS (L-BFGS produced singular-Hessian failures on a subset of edges, silently dropping tests).
  • Outlier screen (|z|>3 delta) applied to all significant features; fragile effects are flagged in the tabs.
  • Preliminary — no permutation max-T at the summary level, no split-half replication.
  • EC results non-causal; spectral DCM (SPM) would be the confirmatory step.
